paragraphs: R’ Yose, son of R’ Simon.

Hyman cites Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni 4:2: R’ Yose says in the name of R’ Yehoshua ben Levi, “For second tithe whose added fifth is not worth a perutah, one does not add a fifth.” In Yalkut Tehillim (remez 760 in the supplied text), Hyman likewise has R’ Yose son of R’ Simon say in the name of R’ Yehoshua ben Levi: “Formerly your name was Israel,” etc. But Pesikta de-Rav Kahana 108b reads R’ Yehudah son of R’ Simon. It appears to Hyman that this SHOULD ALSO BE THE READING in Tanchuma, Vaera 1, and in the Jerusalem Talmud there.

notes.text: ריב״ל denotes Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi here, not Resh Lakish. The checked Maaser Sheni 4:2 attributes the fifth-perutah ruling to Rabbi Yohanan, whereas Hyman supplies ריב״ל. The difference is retained rather than harmonized. His Yosi-toYehudah correction remains a proposal.

No new primary scalar was returned. ריב״ל contextually denotes Yehoshua ben Levi, not the older erroneous Resh Lakish expansion. The earlier recorded Maaser Sheni comparison instead names Yochanan; that attribution difference remains unresolved. The threshold concerns the VALUE OF THE FIFTH, not a perutah beyond it. תש״ס has inherited editorial provenance; 108b remains the conventional supplied locator, not a newly checked edition. Hyman’s IT APPEARS IT SHOULD READ Yehudah rather than Yose remains his qualified proposal. Uninspected abbreviated titles stay R’.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni 4:2:3 attributes the fifth-value ruling to R’ Yochanan through R’ Yose son of R’ Simon. The preceding discussion gives a separate principal-value ruling attributed to R’ Simai through R’ Yaakov bar Idi. The Bava Metzia 4:5:3 parallel gives the fifth-value ruling in the name of R’ Yannai, transmitted by R’ Yochanan. Hyman’s print (vol. II, p. 734) gives תש״ם for the Yalkut reference, and the supplied text gives תש״ס (760). The consulted Yalkut 760 and Tanchuma Buber Vaera 1 name R’ Yose son of R’ Simon without the explicit Yehoshua ben Levi chain. Buber’s Pesikta 108b and the consulted Pesikta 12:23 name R’ Yehudah son of R’ Simon in the name of R’ Yehoshua ben Levi. Hyman proposes extending that reading to the other sources.
